text:
incident-bot: ALERT: realtime.slo.p99 spike detected in eu-west-1 streaming tier. p99 > 2.5s for last 5m, burst from 18:03 UTC
sarah (oncall): on it. joining bridge, will triage. @mike @anya if you're nearby pls standby
mike: I'm on. pulling up grafana dashboards now — links: https://grafana.company/realtime/streaming-latency
mike: quick check: queue depth looks normal, but tail latency heatmap shows a cluster of spikes on node pool A (gpu-pool-a)
anya: customer-impact? any error increases?
leo: customer metrics show increased stream stalls (~0.3%) and retry rate up 0.6% — not yet an SRE page to customers but trending
sarah (oncall): ok runbook step 1: validate KV cache hit-rate and prefix cache eviction
mike: running curl to on-host exporter:
```
curl -s http://10.20.30.5:9100/metrics | egrep 'kv_cache_hit|prefix_cache_ev'
kv_cache_hits_total 124523
kv_cache_misses_total 9873
prefix_cache_evictions_total 432
```
mike: kv hit rate ~92%, eviction spike around 18:02
anya: could be cache thrash on long-tail requests, maybe new prompt patterns
sarah (oncall): mitigation options: 1) temporarily divert traffic off gpu-pool-a -> route to fallback pools 2) enable aggressive prefix caching TTL 3) rollback recent model variant if rolled
leo: I'll start route diversion, Mike can you bump route weight off pool A to 10% and enable overflow to gpu-pool-b
mike: doing now:
```
# set routing weight
redwoodctl routes update realtime --pool gpu-pool-a=10 --pool gpu-pool-b=80 --overflow=true
```
mike: applied, checking
infra-bot: ROUTE_CHANGE: realtime routing updated by mike at 18:06 UTC
mike: metrics already showing p99 moving down to 1.6s in 30s
anya: nice, keep an eye on stalls — if stalls persist, enable per-tenant KV warmup for affected customers
sarah (oncall): any evidence of ongoing backend degradation? storage IO or kernel logs?
leo: checked node logs, some OOM-killers on a few LLM-worker pods ~18:01 but restart count low. Could be transient memory pressure from cache eviction
mike: I'll add a temporary autoscale bump for gpu-pool-b to absorb more headroom
mike: autoscale command:
```
redwoodctl autoscale set gpu-pool-b --min 6 --max 20
```
infra-bot: AUTOSCALE: gpu-pool-b min=6 max=20 by mike
sarah (oncall): good. can ops prod team confirm no customer-facing SLOs breached? Anya?
anya: we've got a few slow initial responses for a handful of heavy customers but not full outage. I'll message CSMs with a heads-up
sarah (oncall): ok we'll keep monitoring. next steps: keep route diversion for 15m, watch p95/p99, investigate model variant rollouts and KV warmup logs. if p99 > 2s again escalate to page
leo: noted, watching dashboards and logs. will follow up with post-incident notes
mike: p99 back to ~1.2s after diversion and autoscale, stalls dropping
sarah (oncall): thanks team. I'll mark incident as active-monitoring. reassign to eng-runtime for deeper follow-up
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: status=active_monitoring, owner=sarah, severity=sev3
sarah (oncall): final: leave diversion until 18:22 UTC, then revert if stable. tagging for postmortem: kv-cache, routing-policy, autoscale-behavior
mike: :thumbsup:
anya: :+1:
leo: :thumbsup:
sarah (oncall): closing bridge, will post notes in #postmortems later tonight
